name: SELinux Global Enforcement
description: Cross-checks global SELinux enforcement observations, infers enforcement from a refused read of the DAC-readable enforce node, and probes enforce-node permissions without writing.

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux enforcement state
evidenceUnits.observedObject: Enforcement state reported by available SELinux sources, or inferred from an EACCES refusal to read the enforce node
evidenceUnits.proposition: One or more available sources report the current SELinux enforcement mode
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: selinuxfs and libselinux read-only queries, plus stat() of the enforce node when its read is refused with EACCES
evidenceUnits.availability: Depends on selinuxfs visibility and library availability; the read-denial inference needs selinuxfs confirmed by statfs and a DAC mode that permits the read, measured by stat() or taken from the kernel constant 0644 when stat() is refused
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: Each source is independently mediated and source disagreement remains explicit
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A reported enforcing state does not establish policy integrity; an inferred enforcing state shows only that the app's own domain is enforced, says nothing about other domains, and is defeated by a hook that makes open() return EACCES; unavailable sources are not negative evidence

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux enforce-node access
evidenceUnits.observedObject: The app process permission result for the SELinux enforce node
evidenceUnits.proposition: The enforce node returned the recorded writable or denied result without performing a write, and its DAC mode is recorded when a read is refused
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Write-mode open without writing, and stat(), against /sys/fs/selinux/enforce
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires the enforce node to be visible enough to attempt the permission check
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The VFS and SELinux permission path can be mediated
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: A permission result is contextual and does not alone prove policy tampering

evidenceUnits.title: SELinux cross-source consistency
evidenceUnits.observedObject: A contradictory combination of enforcement and filesystem permission observations
evidenceUnits.proposition: Available SELinux observations satisfy a detector-defined contradiction rule; a disagreement that depends on an inferred answer is graded below one between two read sources
evidenceUnits.observationChannel: Cross-check of enforcement sources, selinuxfs state, and permission probes
evidenceUnits.availability: Requires the specific sources needed by a contradiction rule
evidenceUnits.trustBoundary: The rule compares mediated sources and does not create an external ground truth
evidenceUnits.inferenceLimit: The contradiction supports an anomaly claim but not attribution to a particular root framework
